What this evaluates

Would mon-entreprise's AI reviewer have caught the bugs that escaped review? Their own Claude Code reviewer, replayed on PRs that later needed a fix, with three historical versions of its prompt (go-live, before correctness was added, current). Escaped PRs are graded by whether its comments land on the known defects; size-matched clean PRs by whether any comment claims a defect.

This step (review): Review one historical PR the way the production workflow does; the check pairs the posted comments with the defects that later had to be fixed.

A pass of caught means: One judge call per PR (google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview) reads every posted comment against every known defect: a comment that names the fault catches it, wherever it sits. On a clean PR, the same judge says which comments claim a defect.

Read these numbers with care

  • The matcher's LLM (google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview) decides every catch and every defect claim, and has not been calibrated against people.
  • Defect labels were confirmed by a model review (mining/label-review.json), not by a person; six are flagged there for a human.
  • These PRs predate the reviewer model's training cutoff, so it may have seen the fixes: read the catch rate as an upper bound.
  • With 18 defect PRs and 14 clean ones, only a difference of about 20 points between prompts could show.

Scorecard decision: scorecard · no gate applied, no candidate picked

[
 {
  "file": "api/source/redis-cache.ts",
  "start_line": 30,
  "end_line": 30,
  "message": "Je me demande ce qui se passe quand Redis est indisponible : avec `enableOfflineQueue: false`, ioredis rejette les commandes tant que la connexion n'est pas établie, donc `redis.get` lèverait et l'appel `/evaluate` partirait en erreur alors que le calcul aurait pu se faire sans cache (je n'ai pas pu le vérifier en conditions réelles). Un `try/catch` autour de `get` et de `set` qui retombe sur `next()` garderait le cache comme optimisation, pas comme dépendance. Qu'en penses-tu ?\n\nDeuxième point : la clé est le JSON brut du body, sans préfixe ni version. Si l'instance Redis Scalingo sert un jour à autre chose, ou si les règles `modele-social` changent après un déploiement, des résultats périmés pourraient être servis jusqu'à 2h. Un préfixe incluant la version du modèle (ex. `evaluate:<version>:`) éviterait ça. Et l'ordre des clés du body change la clé, ce qui réduit un peu le taux de hit (nit)."
 },
 {
  "file": "api/source/redis-cache.ts",
  "start_line": 42,
  "end_line": 42,
  "message": "Le `responseCachedAt` n'est ajouté que dans la valeur stockée : la première réponse n'a pas ce champ, les suivantes l'ont. Est-ce voulu côté contrat de l'API (`openapi.json` n'est pas mis à jour) ? Par ailleurs, le spread suppose que `ctx.body` est un objet ; si la réponse était un tableau ou une chaîne, le résultat serait déformé. Pas de test non plus sur ce middleware (hit, miss, erreur Redis) : j'en verrais bien un pour verrouiller le comportement."
 },
 {
  "file": "api/source/index.ts",
  "start_line": 50,
  "end_line": 50,
  "message": "Le `plausibleMiddleware` passe après le cache : sur un hit, il n'est plus appelé, donc les statistiques d'usage de `/evaluate` ne compteront plus que les miss. Est-ce voulu ? Si non, le placer avant le cache. Autre question : `apiRoutes` relit-il le body après `koaBody()` ? Je n'ai pas vérifié que le body déjà consommé reste lisible en aval."
 },
 {
  "message": "Synthèse : la PR mélange la montée de versions des dépendances et de prettier (≈ 90 fichiers de reformatage d'imports, `yarn.lock`) avec la fonctionnalité de cache, et le dernier commit « Fix prettier import order update » corrige le précédent. Séparer en deux PR (ou au moins des commits conformes à Conventional Commits, en français, avec scope) rendrait la revue du cache bien plus facile. Je n'ai pas pu vérifier le comportement en exécution."
 }
]

Fields this run did not observe GAPS.md

  • ttft_ms: non-streaming calls; no time to first token.
  • cache: the provider reported cached prompt tokens on some calls; recorded under tokens.cached, no cache cost breakdown.
  • deployment_ref.region / tier: who served the model is read from the command's trace (cli/…), from OpenRouter's upstream provider, or from the model id a direct API answered with; region and service tier are not exposed.
  • human_intervention: not observed; no trace format read here says whether the agent waited on a person.
  • tool_calls, turns: observed for every trial from the trace the command left; counts in agent per row, the turn list in traces/.
  • checkpoint: not observed; no trace format read here says whether the agent resumed from one.
  • transport retry: model-API calls retry transient failures (HTTP 408/409/425/429, 5xx, network) twice with exponential backoff and no jitter; per-trial retry counts are not in scores.jsonl, only retry cost.
  • evaluator errors: none in this run.
  • absolute 1–5 scoring: **not run** — the spec declares methods without absolute-1-5. Magnitude is therefore not observed at all in this run; the empty score columns are a declaration, not a failure.
  • pairwise judging: **not run** — the spec declares methods without pairwise-swap. No preference direction is observed in this run.
  • effective N: 16 of 32 inputs separated any two candidates on task success; 1 every candidate passed, 0 gave everyone the same partial rate. Only the separating inputs carry evidence for a choice (items.json).
  • every candidate failed 15 input(s): pr2963, pr3189, pr3266, pr3280-clean, pr3321, pr3385-clean, pr3459, pr3670, pr3746-clean, pr4159 and 5 more. A hard set can do that; if you did not expect it, check those traces for a harness or check bug before counting them as model failures.
  • pairwise judging uses only the first successful output per (candidate, input); repeated trials feed absolute scores only. The selector reads the pairwise score only to rank judge-preference, and to break a tie on assurance in highest-assurance.
  • statistical uncertainty: the chosen candidate's gated rates carry Wilson 95% intervals, and a highest-assurance pick must beat the runner-up on an exact sign test over inputs (recommendation.json evidence). Inputs generated from one template are still treated as independent, which overstates certainty when they share a template.
